storyline.label: MCP Servers
storyline.latest_title: AI coding agents are installing abandoned MCP servers with known security issues

prior_narrative.tldr: On Nov 1 a benchmark post reported a 17-point gap between agents running the same model across 21 MCP servers, putting the client side of MCP under scrutiny. On Nov 2 a Show HN project proposed cryptographic identity for agents calling MCP servers.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Uber built an MCP Gateway to govern agent access to more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools, separating tool registration from runtime execution.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: MCP is moving from per-server wiring to centrally governed infrastructure, and results depend on the agent client as much as the model or server.

status.detail: Threads on MCP agent variance, agent identity and enterprise gateways are emerging together.

beats.headline: Same model, different agent: 17 points apart on 21 MCP servers
Arken proposes cryptographic identity for agents calling MCP servers
Uber centralizes access behind an MCP Gateway

open_questions: Will other large engineering orgs publish MCP gateway designs for discovery, auth and auditing?
Will the 17-point agent-client gap be reproduced on other MCP server sets?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Pin the agent client alongside the model in MCP evals, and check whether tool registration, auth and audit are centralized before your server count grows.
